Synopsis:
    U.S.-Iran military exchanges are pushing crude toward $95/bbl, with Strait of Hormuz tanker traffic disrupted following Iranian attacks. Separately, oil majors signed new energy agreements in Venezuela to revive production (currently ~1.25m bpd), while Trump unveiled a controversial 100-year NABEP lease over 17 Venezuelan oilfields covering ~65bn barrels. Both storylines carry meaningful supply-side uncertainty for global crude markets.
